title: Prevent Earlier, Recognize Sooner, Treat Faster: A Proposed Evidence-Based Medicine–Integrated Rapid Response Framework (EBM-IRRF) for Acute Aortic Dissection
Recent advances in the application of MOF-based adsorbents for toxic dye removal from wastewater and their mechanism
author_affiliation: Wuhan University of Technology, Department of Materials Science and Engineering
co_authors: Maira Aslam, Laiba, Muhammad Zain Ashiq, Ayesha Noreen, Muhammad Imtiaz
abstract:
The increasing influx of pollutants from various sources continues to complicate wastewater treatment processes. Over the past few decades, water contamination has surged, presenting one of the most challenging environmental issues globally. Understanding the underlying chemistry is essential for identifying structural characteristics that can be adjusted to enhance material properties. This review systematically consolidates and critically examines recent breakthroughs (2018-2024) in the use of notable MOF families, such as ZIFs, MILs, and UiO-series, for the removal of cationic (e.g., Methylene Blue) and anionic (e.g., Congo Red) dyes. We focus on understanding the main adsorption mechanisms, including electrostatic interactions, π-π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and coordinative interactions, which frequently work together.
Our study demonstrates that several of these MOFs have extraordinary adsorption capabilities, often exceeding 1000 mg/g, and reach equilibrium in minutes. Furthermore, we assess the important characteristics of MOF stability and regeneration potential, focusing on frameworks that maintain high efficiency across repeated adsorption-desorption cycles. It represents comparison tables for various adsorbents (MOFs) for cationic and anionic dye removal, their adsorption capacity, efficiency, reusability, optimum pH, and temperature. However, it offers insight into current trends in MOF adsorption of dyes and discusses thoroughly factors affecting the dye adsorption on MOFs and mechanisms for removing the dyes from MOFs.
This critical review lays out a clear path for future research aimed at practical implementation, concluding that although MOFs constitute a paradigm change in adsorption science, their translational potential is still limited by scalability and cost issues.
keywords: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs); Dye adsorption; Wastewater treatment; Cationic dyes; Anionic dyes; Adsorption mechanism.
